title: Proverbs 26
paragraphs: ¹ Like snow in summer or rain at harvest, honor is not fitting for a fool. ² Like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow, an undeserved curse does not land. ³ A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools! ⁴ Do not answer a fool according to their folly, or you yourself will be just like them. ⁵ Answer a fool according to their folly, or they will think themselves wise.

⁶ Sending a message through a fool is like cutting off your own feet or drinking poison. ⁷ Like useless legs that hang limp is a proverb in the mouth of a fool. ⁸ Like tying a stone in a sling is giving honor to a fool. ⁹ Like a thorn that goes into the hand of a drunkard is a proverb in the mouth of a fool. ¹⁰ Like an archer who wounds at random is whoever hires a fool or a passerby.

¹¹ As a dog returns to its vomit, so fools repeat their folly. ¹² Do you see someone who thinks themselves wise? There is more hope for a fool than for them. ¹³ A lazy person says, "There is a lion in the road, a fierce lion roaming the streets!" ¹⁴ As a door swings on its hinges, so a lazy person turns over in bed. ¹⁵ A sluggard buries their hand in the dish; they are too tired to bring it back to their mouth.

¹⁶ The sluggard thinks themselves wiser than seven people who give sensible answers. ¹⁷ Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is someone who meddles in a quarrel not their own. ¹⁸ Like a maniac shooting flaming arrows of death ¹⁹ is someone who deceives their neighbor and then says, "I was only joking!" ²⁰ Without wood, a fire goes out; without a gossip, conflict dies down.

²¹ As charcoal to embers and as wood to fire, so is a quarrelsome person for kindling strife. ²² The words of a gossip are like tasty morsels; they go down into the depths of a person. ²³ Like a clay pot coated with cheap silver glaze are fervent lips with an evil heart. ²⁴ Enemies disguise themselves with their lips, but in their hearts they harbor deceit. ²⁵ Though their speech is charming, do not believe them, for seven abominations fill their heart.

²⁶ Their malice may be concealed by deception, but their wickedness will be exposed before the whole assembly. ²⁷ Whoever digs a pit will fall into it; if someone rolls a stone, it will roll back on them. ²⁸ A lying tongue hates those it hurts, and a flattering mouth works ruin.
